A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dual score matching work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. V2's Appendix D image galleries are retained as D.1 in v3, followed by new analyses.

before.justification: V2 reports original Gaussian-mixture experiments, ImageNet64 denoising and likelihood results, generalization tests, and analyses of image probabilities and effective dimensionality.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds CelebA and CIFAR-10 evaluations, image-interpolation experiments, and probability-optimization case studies in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The dual score matching losses, inner-product energy architecture, noise conditioning, and normalization procedure are retained. Appendix D.2 explicitly uses the existing architecture and objective; the new experiments analyze the same method.

E1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds training and evaluation on CelebA in grayscale and color and on CIFAR-10. This substantially broadens the empirical data coverage beyond the retained ImageNet64 and synthetic Gaussian-mixture experiments.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains Glow, PixelCNN, I-DDPM, VDM, FM, NFDM, and TarFlow. The score-network comparison in Table 1 and single-score-matching controls in Figure 1 are unchanged. Appendix D introduces no additional model comparators.

E3.justification: Existing experimental settings are retained. New protocols evaluate interpolations between consecutive example images and perform 1,000 gradient ascent/descent steps with step size 10^-2/d, pixel clipping to [0,1], and selection of the most extreme-probability iterate (Figures 12–13).

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a substantial suite of diagnostics: testing the Gumbel observation across datasets and examining outliers, probing the energy landscape along image interpolations, and examining images obtained by maximizing or minimizing probability. These analyses were absent from v2.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed, and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged. The new histograms reuse maximum-likelihood Gumbel fitting already documented in Appendix C.3; v3 adds no confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figures 9–13 add substantial results: less precise Gumbel fits on the added datasets, interpolation-related probability decreases for medium/high-probability examples and slight increases for low-probability examples, and smoothing, artifacts, or optimization failures during probability maximization. Existing numerical results remain unchanged, including Tables 1–2 and the proposed method's ImageNet64 NLL of 3.36 bits/dimension.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 revises the homogeneity comparison for squared-norm energies from homogeneity with respect to parameters θ to homogeneity with respect to the score function sθ. This changes the object whose scaling is discussed in the mathematical justification. The numbered equations and Appendix B proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the core contributions: normalized energy estimation through dual score matching, competitive ImageNet64 likelihood, strong generalization, and image-dependent probability and dimensionality. Editorial refinements and added supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations linking poorer Gumbel fits to dataset outliers, interpolation behavior to image superposition and contrast, and optimization failures to numerical instability. Section 3.2 adds a non-convex-support interpretation, but its statement that interpolation typically increases probability conflicts with Figure 12's decreases for medium/high-probability images. Existing normalization, theoretical-guarantee, and training-cost limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix D documents reuse of the existing hyperparameters and supplies iteration counts, step size, clipping, and iterate-selection details for probability optimization. Appendix C and code/model access information are unchanged. Table 1's added intensity-range description repeats information already present in Appendix C.2.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged, as are the substantive relationships to earlier and concurrent score-matching, energy-modeling, and dimensionality-estimation work.

P1.justification: V3 polishes sentences throughout the main text, clarifies explanations of the objectives and image information content, and reorders the discussion's limitations and geometry paragraphs. Appendix D is renamed 'Additional results' and subdivided, with the original galleries retained as D.1.

P2.justification: V3 substantially expands the visual evidence through three dataset histogram/example displays, an interpolation plot with image sequences, and an optimization image grid (Figures 9–13). Figures 1–8 and both tables are retained, with limited caption and placement adjustments.

improvement.justification: Appendix D improves scrutiny of the previously ImageNet-focused geometric observations: additional datasets expose limits of the Gumbel fit, while interpolation and optimization tests reveal landscape behavior and failure cases. These are useful empirical qualifications, with the core method and validation unchanged. The gain is partly offset by the new inconsistency between Section 3.2's interpolation summary and Figure 12, limiting the improvement in clarity and reliability.
